mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening consumer demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which lowers earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent decline in the 3-month Treasury bill rate (proxied by FEDFUNDS and implied short rates) signals an aggressive easing cycle, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and implied short rates falling
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 100,000 in a month signals a significant labor market downturn, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by > 100,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the real savings rate (proxied by RSAFS/GDPC1) above its long-run average for six consecutive months signals a shift toward precautionary saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 > long-run average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).
